title: I've been working on my space shooter some more, give it a try!
author: RealAstropulse
selftext:
Been building this game for a while, started out using Antigravity, but the limits were awful and the google models kept changing how they behaved too frequently, swapped to Claude code for everything, much easier to work with. Assets are made with Retro Diffusion.

  
You can play it here: [https://astropulse.github.io/nova-play/](https://astropulse.github.io/nova-play/)

  
I'd love to hear some feedback. The controls/style/gameplay is mostly set now, but some of the systems are up for tweaking. Most of the achievements are too easy atm, planning a larger balance pass for those down the road.

  
Some of the changes since last time I showed it off here:

* Enemies, bosses, and difficulty scaling in general have been overhauled.
* It's got a level up system that lets you choose different bonuses. 
* You can find caches in space, with random rolls of upgrades. 
* It supports controller inputs for the gameplay and menus (feels pretty good too, in my opinion). 
* There are a few bosses to fight, I have plans to add more. 
* There is a whole set of achievements to get and a system for tracking them, it saves them to local storage so they will persist between reloads.
* Caches are delivered at the end of each wave.
* Most upgrades can be combined together up to legendary tier (helps with inventory space a lot).

  
The development progress for this has been pretty satisfying. I committed to solely relying on AI for all the code and art as an experiment, and I'm quite happy so far. None of the systems were too hard to get feeling good and making the assets has been easy. Some of the boss mechanics were hard to nail down, no AI models do well with open-ended tasks like "make a high speed boss fight" so you really need to nail down the specific mechanics for it before telling the AI what to do.

It's not using any kind of engine, just plain JS+HTML, I think this has been a good decision since it's not a particularly demanding game, and AI models are far better at interfacing with languages directly rather than through engines.

comments.author: interestingsystems
comments.body:
This is pretty cool.  
  
One thing I would try changing is the shop - it's currently on the same layer as the asteriods, which feels odd to me, like I should bump into it when I fly over it. If it was on a lower layer, then the parallax would make me realize I can't collide.
